clue.text: Greek mountain bones

definitions.meaning: Mount ... is a peak in Thessaly, piled on Pelion by the giants in myth
the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone

explanation.surface: A note about skeletal remains found on a Greek peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is both a named Greek peak and the Latin anatomical plural meaning bones.

clue.text: Underwear that's annoying

definitions.meaning: a pair of drawers or pants worn under clothing
an exclamation of irritation in British slang, like 'damn!'

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that their undergarments are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'Knickers!' is an exclamation of annoyance, as well as the word for women's pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's pants, and the word is also a mild British expletive voicing exasperation.

clue.text: Physicist who had a real "light bulb" moment saw out Newton

definitions.text: Physicist who had a real "light bulb" moment

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of saw are put out of order

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A physicist with a bright idea saw off Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Swan developed an incandescent light bulb, so the quoted 'light bulb' moment is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Swan, the English physicist and chemist, produced an early working incandescent electric lamp.

clue.text: Dotty Perkins comprehends Latin for "baptise"

indicators.note: comprehends means contains, so one piece takes in the other
dotty means crazy, so the letters of Perkins are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eccentric Mr Perkins understands the Latin word for christening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' scrambles PERKINS into SPRINKE, and 'comprehends' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism can be performed by scattering drops of water over the person, so to baptise is to sprinkle.

clue.text: New age, ground-breaking spear carrier?

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the turf piece is broken into by the other

parts.note: sod is turf, a piece of ground

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of age

explanation.surface: A New Age pioneer carrying a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground-breaking' reads as one adjective but splits: the ground is broken into. The definition is cryptic: Poseidon or Neptune carries a trident.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity of the oceans such as Neptune is pictured holding a trident, a pronged spear.

clue.text: Country representative dances, head to foot a party queen

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is sent down to the bottom, as in a down clue

parts.note: sambas are Brazilian dances
a do is a party
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A national envoy dances about at a party, hailing a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to foot' means the leading letter is sent to the end; R for queen comes from Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a diplomat who represents their nation abroad.

clue.text: Technically, a hoof is a northerner's ear bent back under large body

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits under the second, coming after it

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a large international body

indicators.note: bent back means turned around, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: lug is a northern English and Scottish word for an ear

explanation.surface: A pedantic remark that a hoof is technically a northerner's ear folded backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent back' reverses the pair 'a' plus the ear word together; 'under' places them below the large body in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungula is the zoological term for a hoof, claw or nail.

clue.text: Mischief, latitude and craft

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A list of nautical topics: pranks, navigation and boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, the sort of thing done for mischief.

clue.text: Is working on novel, building literary muscle

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters of is are rearranged

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: A writer working on a novel and building up literary strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like part of the surface's writer at work, but it rearranges only 'Is'; 'building' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinews are tendons, and in literary use the word stands for muscular strength or power.

clue.text: Virgin broadcast by Lisa without one complaint?

indicators.note: broadcast signals a word heard said out loud, then written differently

parts.note: virgin means new, untouched

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Mona goes with Lisa in Leonardo's portrait, the Mona Lisa
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Virgin's broadcaster complains about a Lisa minus one.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling takes a silent P, as in pneumatic. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, wrapping round the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an illness, and lung inflammation is one such ailment.

clue.text: Going like a rocket, when fitted with carbon tip

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a tip is an end; ending here stands in as the extremity

explanation.surface: A rocket being fitted with a carbon nose cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket climbs upward, so going like one means rising or climbing.

clue.text: Africa's principal northerly island in a frenzy

indicators.note: principal means first or leading, so the first letter of Africa is taken

parts.note: Muck is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A frenzied scene on Africa's main island in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Muck is one of the Small Isles off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amuck (amok) is to rush about wildly, in a frenzied rage.

clue.text: Chump acquires modern marketplace, almost leading to reversal of growth

indicators.note: acquires means takes in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a chump, a fool, is a dick in slang

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: eBay is the online auction site

explanation.surface: A fool buys into an online market and nearly sees his growth reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the auction site; 'acquires' places what remains inside the chump.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieback is the progressive death of shoots from the tips, so a plant's growth goes backwards.

clue.text: Broadcaster's changing colour on the way out

indicators.note: a broadcaster's version of a word is the spoken one, heard rather than spelt

parts.note: dyeing is changing the colour of fabric or hair

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's hair is turning a different shade as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the way out is near death or ending, which is to be expiring.

clue.text: NASA's last orbiter with an unstable irregularity

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of NASA
unstable suggests the letters of orbiter and an are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: NASA's latest spacecraft is wobbling with a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' picks the final letter of NASA's, and 'unstable' scrambles the spacecraft plus 'an'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal, an anomaly.

clue.text: See 20
The cast upset very distinctive character

indicators.note: cast here means thrown about, so the letters of the are rearranged
upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A theatre cast is upset by a very distinctive personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges THE into ETH; 'upset' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a group or era.

clue.text: Children's lives appeal

parts.note: lives means exists, the sense of is
to sue is to appeal or plead

explanation.surface: A child's life is a cause for appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring, as in 'died without issue'.

clue.text: See 20
Two seconds to replace the two lengths of lace shawl — a fractional part

indicators.note: to replace says one pair of letters comes in where another stood

parts.note: a mantilla is a Spanish lace scarf worn over the head
L is the abbreviation for length, twice over
S is the abbreviation for second, twice over

explanation.surface: Swapping a lace shawl in just two seconds, with a fraction left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' puts SS where LL stood in MANTILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the mantissa is the decimal part of a logarithm, the bit after the point.

clue.text: Arboreal devastation of Middle East unleashed with such energy

indicators.note: unleashed means let loose, so the letters of Middle East and such are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tree blight from the Middle East unleashed with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unleashed' rearranges MIDDLE EAST and SUCH into DUTCHELMDISEAS, and E ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal blight, spread by beetles, wiped out most mature British elm trees in the 1970s.

clue.text: Element of Subbuteo: call it "Mexican temple"

indicators.note: Element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone names a part of a table football game after a Mexican temple.
explanation.walkthrough: Subbuteo is a British tabletop football game played by flicking small figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A teocalli is an Aztec temple built atop a stepped pyramid in ancient Mexico.

clue.text: Rabbit illusion: disappearance of tail, of stomach

parts.note: to rabbit is to chatter on, which is also to gas

indicators.note: the tail, the last letter, vanishes from the word

parts.note: a trick is an illusion, as in a conjuring trick

explanation.surface: A magician's rabbit trick in which the tail vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' (British slang: to talk on and on) is GAS; 'disappearance of tail' cuts TRICK to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the adjective for anything relating to the belly's digestive organ.

clue.text: Keeping neutral, shoot well

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a sprig is a small shoot or twig
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear stick

explanation.surface: Staying neutral, a marksman shoots well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like an adverb on 'shoot', but it is the noun: a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a natural source of water rising from the ground, like a well.

clue.text: Silly, gimmicky time announcer

definitions.meaning: a novelty clock with a bird popping out to call the hours

explanation.surface: A daft gadget that tells the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means crazy in slang, and also names the bird whose call novelty clocks imitate on the hour.

clue.text: Channel indicator stuck between numerous limits

indicators.note: stuck between means placed in the gap between two letters
limits are the edges, so the first and last letters of numerous are taken

parts.note: an arrow is a pointer or indicator

explanation.surface: A TV channel indicator wedged between many limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' takes N and S, the ends of NUMEROUS, and 'stuck between' puts ARROW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrows is a strait, a slim stretch of water joining two larger bodies, as a channel does.

clue.text: Tree on the way ahead

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tree standing on the road in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To come first is to be in front, ahead of all others.

clue.text: Bombardment of loveless resentment

indicators.note: loveless means without love, and love is the zero letter O in tennis scoring

parts.note: ire is anger or resentment

explanation.surface: A barrage of bitterness from someone unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' removes O (love, a zero score in tennis) from OF, leaving F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is the shooting of guns, so a bombardment is heavy gunfire.

clue.text: Cutting panel for High Street surveyor's use?

parts.note: a clip is a cutting, as from hair or a film
a board is a flat panel, also a committee

explanation.surface: A cutting committee set up to help a shopping-street pollster.
explanation.walkthrough: A High Street (a British town's main shopping street) market researcher stops shoppers with a questionnaire on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A street pollster records answers on a clip-topped writing board, the tool of their trade.

clue.text: Swift sentence?

definitions.meaning: a swift is a fast-flying migratory ...
in British slang a stint in prison is 'doing ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A swift is one example of a feathered creature, and the word is also British slang for prison time.

clue.text: Grace cards

definitions.meaning: to grace is to adorn or decorate

explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or embellish, and a deck is also a full pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Bitter flowed cold and oyster starter turned sour

parts.note: ran means flowed, as a river runs
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of oyster
turned means twisted, so the letters of sour are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sour diner whose oyster starter went off, with cold liquid flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives the first letter of oyster, and 'turned' scrambles 'sour'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of deep-seated bitterness and resentment.

clue.text: Barrel ice houses a thing of the past

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer lies within the words barrel ice

explanation.surface: A barrel of ice holds something from history.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time.
